Kuvitus: hämärässä huoneessa pöydällä on: Illustration: in a dim room, a camera on a tripod stands on a table, and its flash lights up brightly. The light of the flash spreads like a fan to the right towards a flower vase at the end of the table. Next to the camera on the table are two AA batteries, which charge the capacitor of the flash.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: levykondens: Diagram, not to scale: a parallel-plate capacitor connected to a voltage source. On the left is a voltage source with voltage U and the positive terminal at the top. A wire runs from the positive terminal to the left metal plate and from the negative terminal to the right one. The plates stand upright facing each other, and the distance between them is d. On the inner surface of the left plate there are five red positive charges, +Q in total, and on the inner surface of the right plate five blue negative charges, −Q in total. Between the plates there is an insulator, here air, and in it evenly spaced horizontal green field lines whose arrows point from the positive plate to the negative one: a uniform electric field E.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: kaksi kuvaa: Diagram, not to scale: two graphs on a common time axis. Upper: the voltage U_C of the capacitor as a function of time t. In charging the voltage first rises steeply and then ever more gently towards the voltage U_0 of the source, which is marked with a dashed line. In discharging the voltage first drops steeply and then ever more gently towards zero. Lower: the current I. At the start of charging the current is at its greatest and decreases gradually to zero. At the start of discharging the current is again at its greatest but in the opposite direction, that is, negative, and its magnitude decreases gradually to zero. A vertical dashed line separates charging and discharging.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: kaksi saman: Diagram, not to scale: two similar parallel-plate capacitors with the same charge Q: on the left plate five positive charges and on the right plate five negative charges. Between the plates of the left capacitor there is air and four field lines. Between the plates of the right one there is a dielectric whose nine molecules in three rows have become polarised: the negative side of each molecule has turned towards the positive plate and the positive side towards the negative plate. In the dielectric there are only two field lines, so the field is weaker. The voltage U of the capacitor with air is greater, and that of the capacitor with a dielectric is smaller.
Kaavakuva: kondensaattorin jännite U var: Diagram: the voltage U of a capacitor as a function of the charge Q during charging. The graph is a straight line through the origin, because the voltage grows in the same proportion as the charge. Narrow bars are drawn under the line: each represents a small charge that is moved across the voltage at that moment, and the area of the bar is the energy it gains. The bars are low at the start and tall at the end. The triangle between the line and the Q axis is shaded orange; its area is the energy of the capacitor W = ½QU. A horizontal dashed line runs at the average voltage U/2, and the rectangle under it is equal in area to the triangle.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kondensaattorin j: Graph to scale: the voltage U of a capacitor in volts as a function of its charge Q in microcoulombs, grid spacings 10 µC and 2 V. The graph is a straight line that starts at the origin and ends at the point (70 µC; 14 V).
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: toisen kondensaat: Graph to scale: the voltage U of a second capacitor in volts as a function of its charge Q in microcoulombs, grid spacings 20 µC and 1 V. The graph is a straight line that starts at the origin and ends at the point (120 µC; 8 V).
